title: Google's New AI Architecture Changes Everything (Gemma 4 12B)
description:
Google DeepMind just released Gemma 4 12B, a new AI model that completely changes how LLMs process pictures and sound. Instead of running three heavy, separate models at once and slowing down your laptop, it cuts out the middleman to read raw pixels and audio waves directly. In this video, we break down exactly how this new architecture works and why it gives you incredibly fast speeds completely offline.

top_comments.author: @charliegoo1314
top_comments.text: Most commenters missed the point: the Gemma 4 12B isn’t just another LLM—it’s a **small, fully encoder-free multimodal model** that fits comfortably on edge devices. By stripping away heavy vision and audio encoders and letting the language backbone handle all modalities natively, Google has created what’s effectively a **Medium Multimodal Language Model (MMLM)**. This shift signals a major step toward **terminal-based, non-cloud AI**, where powerful multimodal reasoning happens locally on laptops and phones. The future of edge AI is being shaped right now.

top_comments.author: @Gai-i5x

This is odd.  On the latest fully updated LM Studio on Windows 11 for a USB4 tech query I get 26.34 tok/sec in 11 secs for gemma 3 12B and 14.81 tok/sec in 23 secs for gemma 4 12B.  Claude: The Speed vs. Quality Trade-off Explained
This is the key takeaway for your original observation: Gemma 4 is almost certainly running its thinking mode before generating output, silently spending tokens reasoning through how best to structure the answer. You're not seeing those tokens — but you're seeing the result of them. The ~12 extra seconds (23s vs 11s) is very plausibly the thinking budget being consumed before the first visible token appears. The output quality difference strongly supports this hypothesis.
Bottom line: You're not getting slower inference for the same quality — you're getting noticeably better output that costs more compute to produce. Whether that trade-off is worth it depends on your use case, but for a technical explanation like USB4, Gemma 4 wins by a clear margin.
